A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Darwin Gödel Machine study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across pagination changes.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original SWE-bench and Polyglot experiments, baseline comparisons, transfer evaluations, repeated-run statistics, and a hallucination case study.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A, G, and H.

M1.justification: The method and generated-agent implementations are retained. Section 3 corrects selection to be inversely related to child count, matching v2's existing Appendix C.2 formula. Algorithms 1–3 explicitly initialize the base agent's score, documenting evaluation already reported in v2 rather than establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot, including cross-benchmark and programming-language transfer and the hallucination scenario. Advanced-model and generalist-agent extensions in v3's Appendix J remain future work.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the base agent, DGM without self-improvement, DGM without open-ended exploration, DGM Greedy, OpenHands + CodeAct v2.1, and Aider. The added SWE-agent citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Reported task subsets, staged evaluation thresholds, 80-iteration benchmark runs, model assignments, temperature, and pass@1 convention remain unchanged. Appendix H retains its three-task, 150-iteration hallucination experiment. The added documentation does not establish revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: The transfer tests, parent-selection ablation, functional-agent analysis, alternative editing implementations, and hallucination/objective-hacking case study are retained. The added inference-cost observation is not accompanied by a new ablation, sensitivity test, or detailed supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 in both versions reports three Polyglot runs with mean accuracy 40.7% and standard deviation 2.3%. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged, including SWE-bench improvement from 20.0% to 50.0% and full-Polyglot improvement from 14.2% to 30.7%. Appendix E.1 newly reports that stronger evolved agents incur greater inference costs than the initial agent, while some expensive agents underperform cheaper ones; no supporting measurements are added.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 retains the mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(7), including the inverse-child-count novelty factor. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced; the pseudocode initialization clarification adds procedural documentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about self-referential improvement through archive-based exploration, advantages over the baselines, and improvements on both coding benchmarks. The main contribution and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly discusses how stronger foundation models may reduce the value of some scaffolding, why task-specific adaptation is expected, and the limitation of evaluation on only two benchmarks. The Ethics Statement and new Appendix I add qualifications concerning ecosystem bias, deployment, and safety when scaling the system.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 now explicitly evaluate the initial agent and store its agent-score pair. The new Reproducibility Statement specifies planned release of full logs, lineage, configurations, environment specifications, and reproduction scripts. These are additional commitments; the PDFs do not establish newly available artifacts.

R1.justification: Section 2 extends the stated open-ended-exploration distinction to the already cited Zelikman and Yin approaches. Appendix J adds a SWE-agent citation to Yang et al. (2024) when discussing foundation-model advances and scaffolding; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording corrections, changes the author footnote to co-first authors, and moves the parent-selection explanation from Appendix C.2 into Section 3. It adds dedicated Ethics and Reproducibility Statements and safety discussion, with future work becoming Appendix J; most existing prose and organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds conference headers and adjusts spacing and page breaks around figures, prompts, algorithms, and the new statements. Figures 1–8 and the existing tables retain their displays, labels, captions, and contents; the visual changes are limited to layout.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves small documentation inconsistencies by aligning parent-selection wording with the existing formula and explicitly initializing scored archive entries. Its additional reproducibility commitments and specific applicability limitations improve transparency. The empirical evidence is unchanged and the new inference-cost observation remains unquantified, so the overall gain is limited.
